purpose: Teach: 南東/電電/ヴォーカル/長調/小麦粉/エッセー/豪快/マーカー

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが家を南東向きに建てられた
lines.en: You know, dear, back when we were young, your father built the house facing southeast.
lines.style: Low and slow, a long remembering pause before the detail, voice softened by distance.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん、お祖父ちゃん、若い頃、電電公社にお勤めだったわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Yes… and you worked at the old telephone corporation when you were young, didn't you, dear?
lines.style: Papery gentle warmth, slight age-wobble, rising tenderly into the question at the end.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんがバンドのヴォーカルを担当された
lines.en: In those days, your father even sang — he was the vocalist in a band.
lines.style: Quiet marvel in a low register, unhurried, letting the memory surface between phrases.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、若い頃、長調の明るい曲をお好みだったわよね、あなた?
lines.en: And you always favored those bright major-key tunes back then, didn't you, dear?
lines.style: Slow doting lilt, smiling through the memory, the closing question soft as a hand-pat.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが小麦粉、つまりうどん用の粉に詳しかった
lines.en: Your father knew everything about flour in those days — udon flour especially.
lines.style: Dry gentle admiration, measured pace, a faint chuckle buried under the second phrase.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、若い頃、随筆エッセーを書かれたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: You wrote essays yourself when you were young, didn't you, dear?
lines.style: Warm proud hush, slowing on essays, the question curling upward with quiet affection.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが豪快に笑う姿が頼もしかった
lines.en: The way your father laughed back then, so big and hearty — it made you feel everything would be all right.
lines.style: Voice warming and dropping lower, a reverent pause before the final admission of feeling.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、若い頃、マーカーで地図に印を付けられたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: And you used to mark up all our maps with a marker, didn't you, dear?
lines.style: Soft closing chuckle woven through the words, slow and satisfied, settling like a quilt.
